response.markdown_report:
Test **16-negative candidate cross-entropy with the corrected NextItNet architecture fixed**, while strengthening controls before attributing gains to the objective. At 20% progress, this remains more practical than hard-negative retrieval or additional context gates.

Three starting-point insights guide the experiment. First, zero-initialized residual-depth correction preserves the final-state path initially, supporting controlled architecture comparisons. Second, reported scores of 0.5325 and 0.5175 motivate retaining existing features, but lack paired uncertainty. Third, Industrial_and_Scientific and Electronics show 8.22% and 6.67% sampled training misranking. These descriptive observations motivate discrimination experiments without establishing held-out weakness or temporal causes.

Three literature insights refine the methodology. NextItNet and Scalable Cross-Entropy motivate studying candidate competition, but establish no winner here. Di Teodoro et al. show that one-negative candidate CE equals BPR; Wu et al. motivate separating objective, negative count and sampling. PSL and R2NS caution against false negatives and unrestrained hardness, supporting uniform sampling first. MSDCCL motivates later suppression experiments, because changing discrimination does not directly remove stale context.

| Direction | Intervention | Unresolved question |
|---|---|---|
| Representation | Residual-depth correction | Are intermediate depths useful? |
| Discrimination | Multi-negative cross-entropy | Does competition improve specific matches? |
| Context | Causal input suppression | Can stale context be reduced safely? |

Scores are originality/potential/user alignment/model alignment/difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation. Every dimension includes a favorable and unfavorable assessment.

| Idea | Scores | Critical assessment |
|---|---|---|
| **Uniform 16-negative CE** [NextItNet, SCE, Di Teodoro] | 2/6/4/7/4 | Originality: controlled adaptation, established objective. Potential: reusable evidence, uncertain transfer. User: rewards conditional specificity, no explicit forgetting. Model: targets discrimination, training misranking may not generalize. Difficulty: localized change, reproducible exclusions and controls add work. |
| Same-network hard-negative curriculum [R2NS, PSL] | 3/6/5/7/6 | Originality: task-specific adaptation, established curriculum. Potential: informative competition, uncertain negatives. User: challenges broad matches, cannot verify purpose. Model: targets hard margins, may destabilize training. Difficulty: retains one network, retrieval increases cost. |
| Causal convolution-input suppression [MSDCCL] | 4/7/8/6/6 | Originality: family-specific placement, familiar gating. Potential: adaptable context, useful history may disappear. User: targets stale and broad associations, intent remains latent. Model: may improve discrimination, temporal evidence is omitted. Difficulty: localized gates, substantial masking checks. |

Select uniform candidate CE as a feasibility-led hypothesis. It explicitly targets broad associations displacing specific current matches and older secondary interests outranking recent-purpose matches, through stronger conditional discrimination. Both connections are indirect; the second lacks an explicit forgetting mechanism. Measured training misranking supplies the model-facing target, not proof of benefit.

Keep architecture and existing depth aggregation fixed. Compare losses using matched eligible pools and negatives; isolate negative count separately when budget permits. Select solely by pinned four-category macro validation HR@10. Krichene–Rendle show why sampled ranking gains cannot establish full-catalog gains. Compatibility, quantity suitability, duplication, popularity shortcuts and real-user utility remain unresolved.

idea.description: Test cross-entropy over one positive and 16 uniformly sampled, distinct negatives per valid causal position in the host-supplied corrected NextItNet. Preserve its backbone, supplied depth-aggregation configuration, scoring head, optimizer and inference architecture. Use matched sampling controls to distinguish objective effects from changes in negative count or exclusion policy. Each configuration independently trains exactly one network per category; deployment loads exactly one selected checkpoint per category without fusion or averaging.
idea.motivation: Explicit competition among multiple alternatives may improve conditional next-item discrimination. The two user-facing targets are broad associations displacing specific matches to current purpose, and older secondary interests outranking recommendations supported by recent interactions. These are hypotheses rather than demonstrated mechanisms: candidate CE can reward predictive conditioning but introduces neither recency weighting nor explicit forgetting, and it can also exploit item-frequency shortcuts. Its user-diagnosis alignment is therefore weaker than the previous rating suggested. The model-facing target is sampled training misranking, reported as 8.22% in Industrial_and_Scientific and 6.67% in Electronics; these position-weighted training observations do not establish held-out error rates. At 20% progress, a controlled loss experiment remains feasible and informative before adding hard mining or architecture changes. Retain causal input suppression as a separate future hypothesis. Historical proposal scores do not establish that CE will outperform the supplied cold start.
idea.implementation_notes:
This is an integration component because the baseline train.py, sample_batch implementation, ModelView and predictor writer are absent from the prompt. Integrate into the supplied corrected baseline rather than inventing its formats, APIs or training harness. The provided loss and sampler helpers are executable components, but their integration placeholders are not a complete runnable train.py. No training, filesystem inspection or new empirical results are claimed here.

Start every configuration from the host-supplied corrected cold start with training seed 42, never another trial's checkpoint. Preserve the supplied architecture, including its actual depth-correction configuration; do not silently import an architecture from the inspiration history. Keep embedding dimensions, convolution blocks, dilation schedule, normalization, masking, final transformation, scorer, optimizer, regularization and gradient processing unchanged for the initial experiment. Baseline training metadata is needed to determine whether the original objective is BCE, BPR or another loss and how its reductions and negative sampler operate. Record those actual settings rather than assuming them.

Use K=16 and temperature=1.0 as the primary proposed configuration. This is uncorrected candidate classification: -log(exp(s_positive)/(exp(s_positive)+sum(exp(s_negative)))). Do not describe it as an unbiased estimator of full-catalog CE or as a calibrated probability over all items. Excluding a user's complete training-item set changes the denominator support to that user's eligible unseen items. For K draws without replacement from M eligible items, each eligible item's inclusion probability is K/M, but adding a correction cannot restore contributions from excluded items. A constant adjustment to every logit cancels; the guaranteed positive and sampled negatives need separate treatment in any future corrected objective. No sampling correction is introduced in this experiment.

Distinguish end-to-end comparison from component attribution. Comparing the native baseline directly with CE16 changes both objective and sampling whenever the native negative count or exclusions differ. It can establish a configuration difference under the pinned metric, but cannot isolate the loss. Before inspecting new scores, record a budget-feasible comparison order: native baseline, native objective with the same K=16 candidate sets and exclusions as CE16, then CE16. If the native objective has no defensible multi-negative extension, specify that explicitly and use a named averaged-BPR16 control rather than calling it the unchanged native objective. For BPR, average softplus(s_negative-s_positive) across valid negatives per position, then across positions. For BCE, separately average the positive term and valid negative terms per position, then sum them; distinguish this class-balanced form from averaging all K+1 labels. Preserve and report the native reduction in the native baseline. Loss scale and regularization balance remain possible explanations when moving between objectives, even with the same optimizer.

If remaining budget permits a prespecified expansion, add CE1 and the corresponding matched one-negative reference, yielding a loss-by-negative-count comparison. Candidate CE1 equals BPR1 at temperature 1, providing an algebraic implementation check rather than a distinct scientific treatment. Generate the K=16 ordered sample first and use its first item for K=1 so samples are nested. Do not simultaneously sweep temperature, architecture, optimizer, exclusions, replacement policy and correction. Replacement, exclusion and correction are separate later questions. If only native baseline and CE16 fit the remaining budget, retain that narrower comparison and explicitly limit attribution. Do not launch a large factorial design simply because related work recommends comprehensive controls.

Sample from mapped, training-observed item IDs only. Exclude padding ID 0, the current target, and every item in the user's complete permitted training history. Never inspect validation or test interactions for exclusions. Including later interactions within the training partition in the exclusion set is an explicit retrospective sampling convention; it is not a causal input feature or a prospective exposure policy. It avoids known-positive collisions but does not eliminate latent false negatives among unseen items. Exclusions also change negative difficulty and may reward frequency shortcuts, so they must match across controlled losses.

Sample uniformly without replacement within each position. Sequential rejection of historical items and already accepted negatives preserves uniform ordered sampling. Do not sort or truncate np.unique results, which can favor smaller IDs. If fewer than K eligible items exist, return all eligible items in random order, pad remaining slots with zero, and mask those slots. If the pool is empty, skip that position and count it. Such shortage rows have fewer competitors and must be reported separately. Do not manufacture negatives, silently switch to replacement, or loop indefinitely. For sparse exclusions, rejection sampling is efficient; after a fixed proposal limit, draw the remainder uniformly from an explicit eligible complement. This preserves uniformity while bounding rejection work. Avoid caching every user's catalog complement or allocating a user-by-catalog dense matrix. Any lazy complement cache must have a documented memory bound. The supplied helper constructs a transient complement only when needed.

Preserve the baseline's sequence/user sampler RNG state and draw order. Use separate randomness for new negative sampling; equal seeds alone do not preserve the original sequence stream. For worker-count-independent negative sampling, derive a NumPy Generator from a SeedSequence containing fixed identifiers: seed 42, declared category index, epoch, batch index and within-batch row occurrence. If training samples individual positions independently, use stable position-occurrence identifiers instead. Repeated occurrences require distinct deterministic identifiers; do not hash Python objects with the process-randomized built-in hash. Match identifiers across loss controls and exclude configuration names from this seed key. Changes in K or rejection cost must not consume sequence-selection randomness.

When the baseline uses a DataLoader, retain its existing sampling behavior and explicitly record its generator and worker initialization. Seed Python and NumPy worker-local RNGs from torch.initial_seed(); separately initialize any stored NumPy Generator objects. Persistent workers do not rerun worker_init_fn every epoch, so communicate epochs explicitly or use identifier-derived negative generators. Do not replace the baseline generator merely to add a new one. Record worker count, start method, software versions and deterministic settings. Seed 42 does not alone guarantee bitwise GPU reproducibility; report nondeterministic operations or unsupported deterministic kernels without silently changing the backbone. Verify repeated-run negative equality and unchanged sequence choices on a small fixed fixture.

The legacy training/diagnostic loader remains (None, sequence, positive, negative), with B x L tensors. The first field is not a user ID. Obtain user identity inside the existing family-specific sample_batch worker, where the sampled user is known, and generate exclusion-aware negatives before discarding that identity. Alternatively retain private training-only row provenance in the trainer without changing the host diagnostic tuple. Never infer a complete user's exclusion set from a truncated sequence or invent a user_ids field in the host loader. If the supplied baseline does not expose provenance internally, adding that private provenance is a required integration change before this sampler is valid. The helper operates on one position; production code should batch candidates and reuse per-user exclusion sets within the existing CPU workers.

Filter valid positions with nonzero sequence and positive IDs. Score the positive and candidates through the actual model.predict_score used by diagnostics and inference, including any scorer transformations or item biases. Do not substitute raw embedding dot products unless that is exactly the baseline scorer. The loss accepts score tensors to avoid assuming unsupported broadcasting. Candidate adapters must ensure that aligned positive scores have shape N and candidate scores N x K; compare their outputs against individual baseline scorer calls. Mask padding candidate scores out of the loss and mask target positions consistently. Average candidate CE over eligible valid positions, retaining the baseline's position weighting. Keep explicit regularization unchanged and document how its relative magnitude changes with the objective.

To control peak memory, score valid positions in deterministic chunks if necessary. Accumulate summed data-loss gradients divided by the total eligible-position count, then add baseline regularization once and take one optimizer step per original batch. Keep the same feature forward pass and dropout realization when chunking scores; averaging chunk means equally would overweight small chunks. Do not change baseline batch size or updates to accommodate the new loss without reporting that deviation. Record actual negatives per position, skipped positions, optimizer steps, parameter count, peak GPU memory, throughput and GPU-seconds. Empty pools should be exceptional; if an entire batch has no eligible positions, skip its optimizer step and record the departure from nominal update matching.

Preserve all four dataset routes: Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics and CDs_and_Vinyl. DATA_DIR remains os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']. Keep preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, single-GPU execution, maximum 200 epochs and exactly 200 sampled batches per executed epoch. Preserve the historical SASREC_EPOCHS default of 200 and cap execution at 200. Write all artifacts beneath the trial directory. Serialize exact inherited settings, category ordering, RNG keys, exclusions, objective reductions, checkpoint epochs, stopping policy and deterministic tie rule before execution. Keep checkpoint inspection schedules and allocated tuning opportunity matched across complete configurations. Count prior expenditure, training, diagnostics, debugging and failures against the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget. Remaining allowance and timing are not supplied, so feasibility cannot be certified here. Reduce the planned comparison set before inspecting its new scores when timing makes completion infeasible. Never rank a configuration missing any of the four categories.

Inference adds no layer or sampler. Preserve the predictor writer's exact architecture definition and configuration, and strict-load exactly one selected state_dict for the routed category. Save objective and sampling settings as training metadata only. Match training, diagnostic and predictor score computation. Keep item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), view.model as the actual trained nn.Module and every ModelView interface. For left-padded histories, gather the largest nonzero sequence index, never count-1, and use the baseline's empty-history convention. Preserve internal causal padding and masks. Verify strict save/load score agreement, final-position readout, batch reordering and causal behavior without adding a separate inference scorer.

Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device).run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions, and callable diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Keep the family-specific loader contract unchanged. Existing fixed diagnostic negatives should remain matched across model comparisons; do not compare each model using its own changing training negatives. Report measured sampled misranking, margin distributions, valid counts and sampling definitions. Covariance effective rank measures concentration and is not RankMe or proof of harmful collapse. Existing structural recognition remains applicable only while the actual graph is unchanged and recognized. The supplied sensitivity and candidate-depth outputs are omitted; do not infer their values or temporal conclusions.

Popularity shortcuts and memorization remain plausible. Where the existing authorized training diagnostic supports them, measure recommendation frequency/coverage and score sensitivity after shuffling the same histories while retaining final-position handling. Compare behavior by training-item frequency and history length, using common users and candidate pools. These in-sample probes do not establish generalization or semantic specificity. Do not modify the host evaluator or reconstruct validation targets to obtain full-catalog results. Full-catalog validation, target-popularity strata and paired hit analyses are available only if the host already supplies an authorized interface or outputs. The final simulator recommendations for twenty training users remain qualitative evidence, with no auxiliary selection score. Missing diagnostics must be reported as unavailable rather than zero effects.

Select solely by unchanged pinned macro validation HR@10 across four categories, preferring the native baseline on exact ties, then a prespecified lower-cost control on remaining ties. Do not tune on diagnostic training accuracy, simulator judgments or hidden tests. Record every attempted configuration and checkpoint inspection: repeated adaptive use of 800 validation users can overfit the selection set. One changed validation hit changes the four-category macro by 0.00125. If paired outcomes are supplied, report per-category differences, discordant hits and a seed-42 paired user bootstrap within categories with equal category weights; otherwise report paired uncertainty as unavailable. These intervals condition on fitted models and fixed candidates and do not correct adaptive selection, training-seed uncertainty or candidate-sampling variability. Sampled HR@10 can reverse full-catalog model orderings, so benchmark gains cannot establish full-catalog utility. Freeze one selected checkpoint per category and its matching predictor before final held-out evaluation.

Use only permitted public histories, titles, descriptions and timestamps. No reviews, ratings, prices, stores, item-category attributes, unobserved simulator traits, pretrained weights, extra datasets, hard mining, independently fitted transition/popularity scores, or model fusion are introduced. Duplication, exact compatibility, quantity suitability and unmet purchasing demand remain unobserved or unresolved.
idea.pseudocode:
import numpy as np
import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F


CATEGORY_INDEX = {
    'Movies_and_TV': 0,
    'Industrial_and_Scientific': 1,
    'Electronics': 2,
    'CDs_and_Vinyl': 3,
}


def occurrence_rng(category, epoch, batch_index, occurrence_index):
    # Same identifiers across matched loss controls. No Python hash().
    identifiers = [42, CATEGORY_INDEX[category], int(epoch),
                   int(batch_index), int(occurrence_index)]
    if any(x < 0 for x in identifiers):
        raise ValueError('RNG identifiers must be nonnegative')
    return np.random.default_rng(np.random.SeedSequence(identifiers))


def uniform_distinct_negatives(catalog, complete_training_items,
                               target, count, rng):
    """Reference sampler for one valid training position.

    catalog: prevalidated 1-D unique positive training-observed IDs.
    complete_training_items: this user's complete training-item set.
    Returns IDs (count,) and validity mask (count,).
    Production integration should reuse sets and batch worker operations.
    """
    catalog = np.asarray(catalog, dtype=np.int64)
    if catalog.ndim != 1 or count < 1:
        raise ValueError('Expected 1-D catalog and positive count')
    # Validate catalog positivity/uniqueness once at dataset construction.
    forbidden = set(complete_training_items)
    forbidden.add(0)
    forbidden.add(int(target))
    accepted = []
    accepted_set = set()
    proposal_limit = max(64, 8 * count)

    # Preserve acceptance order; never sort np.unique(proposals).
    if len(catalog):
        for _ in range(proposal_limit):
            item = int(catalog[int(rng.integers(len(catalog)))])
            if item in forbidden or item in accepted_set:
                continue
            accepted.append(item)
            accepted_set.add(item)
            if len(accepted) == count:
                break

    if len(accepted) < count:
        # Bounded fallback, transient O(catalog) memory.
        remaining = np.fromiter(
            (int(item) for item in catalog
             if int(item) not in forbidden
             and int(item) not in accepted_set),
            dtype=np.int64,
        )
        take = min(count - len(accepted), len(remaining))
        if take:
            extra = rng.choice(remaining, size=take, replace=False)
            accepted.extend(int(item) for item in extra)

    ids = np.zeros(count, dtype=np.int64)
    valid = np.zeros(count, dtype=np.bool_)
    ids[:len(accepted)] = accepted
    valid[:len(accepted)] = True
    return ids, valid


def matched_candidate_loss(positive_scores, negative_scores,
                           negative_valid, objective='ce',
                           temperature=1.0):
    """Scores come from the unchanged NextItNet predict_score.

    positive_scores: (N,); negative_scores: (N,K).
    Rows represent valid causal training positions.
    Returns mean loss and eligible row count.
    'bce' is explicitly class-balanced, not necessarily native BCE.
    """
    if objective not in ('ce', 'bpr', 'bce'):
        raise ValueError('Unknown objective')
    if temperature <= 0:
        raise ValueError('temperature must be positive')
    if positive_scores.ndim != 1 or negative_scores.ndim != 2:
        raise ValueError('Expected positive (N,) and negative (N,K)')
    if negative_scores.shape[0] != positive_scores.shape[0]:
        raise ValueError('Position counts disagree')
    if negative_valid.shape != negative_scores.shape:
        raise ValueError('Negative mask shape disagrees')
    if negative_valid.dtype != torch.bool:
        raise TypeError('negative_valid must be boolean')

    eligible = negative_valid.any(dim=1)
    count = int(eligible.sum().item())
    if count == 0:
        return positive_scores.sum() * 0.0, 0

    pos = positive_scores[eligible].float() / temperature
    neg = negative_scores[eligible].float() / temperature
    mask = negative_valid[eligible]
    # Remove masked scores before nonlinearities, including possible NaNs.
    neg = neg.masked_fill(~mask, 0.0)
    per_row_count = mask.sum(dim=1).to(pos.dtype)

    if objective == 'ce':
        logits = torch.cat(
            (pos[:, None], neg.masked_fill(~mask, float('-inf'))),
            dim=1,
        )
        labels = torch.zeros(count, dtype=torch.long,
                             device=logits.device)
        return F.cross_entropy(logits, labels), count

    if objective == 'bpr':
        terms = F.softplus(neg - pos[:, None])
        per_row = terms.masked_fill(~mask, 0.0).sum(1)
        per_row = per_row / per_row_count
    else:
        negative_terms = F.softplus(neg).masked_fill(~mask, 0.0)
        per_row = F.softplus(-pos)
        per_row = per_row + negative_terms.sum(1) / per_row_count
    return per_row.mean(), count


# Required integration into the supplied family-specific sample_batch:
# The sampled user is known INSIDE the worker. Generate training-only
# negatives there using that user's COMPLETE training history. Do not
# recover identity from the legacy (None, seq, pos, neg) diagnostic tuple.
# Keep the baseline sequence RNG and its exact draw order unchanged.
# For each valid row/position occurrence, use an identifier-derived RNG.
# Generate ordered K=16 candidates; K=1 controls use the first candidate.
# Preserve legacy loader outputs for ModelView and diagnostic probes.

# Training integration (named adapters below require baseline source):
# features = model.log2feats(sequence)                 # B x L x D
# valid = sequence.ne(0) & positive.ne(0)
# f = features[valid]
# target = positive[valid]
# negative_ids, negative_valid = worker_generated_candidates_for(valid)
# positive_scores = actual_scorer_for_aligned_items(model, f, target)
# negative_scores = actual_scorer_for_candidate_rows(model, f, negative_ids)
# data_loss, count = matched_candidate_loss(
#     positive_scores, negative_scores, negative_valid,
#     objective='ce', temperature=1.0,
# )
# if count:
#     loss = data_loss + unchanged_baseline_regularization(model)
#     optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
#     loss.backward()
#     unchanged_baseline_gradient_processing()
#     optimizer.step()
# else:
#     record_skipped_optimizer_step()
#
# If scoring in chunks, sum per-position losses / GLOBAL eligible count;
# add regularization once, then take ONE optimizer step for the batch.
#
# Essential fixed-fixture checks before costly fitting:
# - all sampled IDs are training-observed, positive, unseen for the user;
# - no within-row duplicates; shortages have correct masks;
# - same occurrence identifiers reproduce candidates across losses/workers;
# - sequence choices match the original sampler stream;
# - CE1 == BPR1, and padding candidate slots do not affect the loss;
# - batch scoring adapters match individual actual predict_score calls.
#
# Inference keeps the supplied architecture and scoring API:
# positions = torch.arange(sequence.shape[1], device=sequence.device)
# last = positions.expand_as(sequence).masked_fill(sequence.eq(0), -1).amax(1)
# nonempty = last.ge(0)
# Handle empty histories using the supplied baseline convention.
# rows = torch.arange(sequence.shape[0], device=sequence.device)[nonempty]
# endpoint = model.log2feats(sequence)[rows, last[nonempty]]
# scores = model.predict_score(endpoint, candidates[nonempty])

# Preserve the embedded predictor writer, strict-loading exactly one
# selected checkpoint for each routed category. The sampler is training-only.
# Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device).run_full_diagnosis(train_loader)
# and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), with measured definitions.
# Select complete four-category configurations only through pinned HR@10.

originality.positive: The experiment connects matched negative sampling, explicit objective reductions and the required NextItNet diagnostic interfaces in a controlled benchmark adaptation.
originality.negative: Candidate cross-entropy and multi-negative training are established, and NextItNet already discusses sampled softmax. The contribution is experimental evidence rather than a new learning principle.

future_potential.positive: Matched controls can establish whether objective choice or candidate competition deserves further investment before adding retrieval or context-selection mechanisms.
future_potential.negative: Uniform negatives may remain easy, unseen items may be relevant, and sampled validation gains can reflect popularity shortcuts. The method offers no direct solution to stale context, compatibility or purchasing intent.

code_difficulty.positive: The backbone, deployed scorer and checkpoint architecture remain unchanged; the core differentiable loss is small.
code_difficulty.negative: Complete-user exclusions require training-worker provenance, while reproducible RNG separation, matched controls, shortage handling and memory-aware scoring make reliable integration more involved than a loss replacement.

related_work.title: NextItNet
contributions: Introduces causal dilated convolutional next-item modeling.
Discusses sampled-softmax scalability as an alternative to full-catalog softmax.
limitations: Does not establish that the proposed 16-negative candidate-classification configuration improves this pinned benchmark.
Does not isolate negative-count effects or establish resistance to popularity shortcuts.
Causal convolution alone does not identify current purchasing purpose.

related_work.title: Scalable Cross-Entropy (RecSys 2024)
contributions: Studies efficient softmax approximation using informative catalog subsets.
The supplied search results describe comparisons of full CE, multi-negative BCE, sampled CE and SCE with unsampled ranking metrics and catalog coverage.
limitations: Its informative-subset method differs from uniform sampling.
Memory-budget comparisons can vary batch size and sampling settings, preventing a negative-count-only interpretation.
Results using SASRec do not establish gains for the supplied NextItNet task or prove popularity debiasing.

related_work.title: PSL (NeurIPS 2024)
contributions: Examines softmax sensitivity to false negatives and alternative pairwise activations.
The supplied search results describe injected false-negative and popularity-shift controls.
limitations: Excluding observed positives does not eliminate uncertain relevance among unobserved items.
Collaborative-filtering experiments do not directly validate this NextItNet objective.
Hardness and false-negative robustness cannot be inferred from the supplied training margins alone.

related_work.title: R2NS (WWW 2026)
contributions: Motivates uniform warm-up before curriculum-controlled hard-negative retrieval.
Ablations described in the supplied search results emphasize retaining random negatives alongside harder candidates.
limitations: Retrieval, warm-up and hardness schedules add complexity beyond the initial experiment.
Hard negatives can include relevant unobserved items.
The supplied search summary notes unclear sampled-versus-full-catalog evaluation specification, limiting transfer of conclusions.

related_work.title: MSDCCL (2024)
contributions: Combines soft weighting and hard denoising to address noisy sequential context.
Motivates a separate investigation of interaction suppression.
limitations: Weighting can retain irrelevant context, while deletion can remove useful history.
Does not establish that the supplied model's errors arise from stale context.
Candidate cross-entropy does not implement its denoising mechanism.

related_work.title: Di Teodoro et al.: comparison of recommendation objectives
contributions: The supplied search results describe comparisons of BCE, BPR and categorical cross-entropy across multiple datasets and models.
Supports distinguishing objective choice from candidate count; one-negative candidate CE equals BPR at temperature 1.
limitations: Does not establish a NextItNet-specific winner for these four datasets.
Objective comparisons require explicit reductions, matched sampling and comparable tuning opportunities.

related_work.title: Wu et al.: sampled-softmax recommendation study
contributions: The supplied search results describe separate ablations of negative count, sampling distribution and in-batch sampling.
Includes multiple-negative BCE/BPR controls relevant to isolating candidate competition.
limitations: Results do not determine the optimal loss or negative count for the pinned NextItNet benchmark.
Different loss reductions can change gradient scale and class weighting.

related_work.title: Blanc and Rendle: adaptive sampled softmax
contributions: Analyzes sampling distributions and bias in sampled-softmax training.
Provides context for distinguishing corrected full-softmax approximation from uncorrected candidate classification.
limitations: Sampling corrections do not generally make finite-sample gradients unbiased.
User-specific exclusion support cannot represent an unrestricted denominator without restoring omitted contributions.

related_work.title: Khrylchenko et al.: sampled-softmax analysis
contributions: The supplied search results identify this work as further analysis of sampled-softmax objectives and correction.
limitations: Does not directly validate the proposed uncorrected, exclusion-aware candidate loss.
Exact correction formulas depend on the sampling process and treatment of the guaranteed positive.

related_work.title: Krichene and Rendle: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled recommendation metrics can disagree with full-catalog metrics, including model-order reversals.
limitations: Does not invalidate the stipulated sampled benchmark as its own selection objective.
Does not supply an authorized full-catalog validation interface for this task.

related_work.title: NumPy Generator.choice documentation
contributions: Documents uniform sampling without replacement and eligible-population constraints.
limitations: Does not implement per-user history exclusions or define the experiment's shortage policy.
Reproducibility also depends on generator initialization and draw order.

related_work.title: PyTorch data loading guidance
contributions: Provides data-loading context for dedicated generators, worker seeds and worker-local initialization.
limitations: Worker seeding alone does not preserve an existing sampler's draw order.
Persistent workers and dataset-owned NumPy Generators require explicit handling.

related_work.title: NumPy parallel random generation
contributions: Documents SeedSequence-based separate streams and deterministic identifier-based initialization.
limitations: Worker-independent reproducibility requires stable occurrence identifiers chosen by the application.
Independent sampler streams do not guarantee bitwise deterministic GPU training.
